pr_title: Add CSI block volume directory cleanup
pr_body:
CSI volume plugin creates number of files/directories when processing block volumes. These files must be cleaned when the plugin is done with the volume, i.e. at the end on `TearDownDevice` or when `SetupDevice` fails.

I added unit tests covering both `SetupDevice` failure and full lifetime of a CSI block volume from `SetupDevice` trough `MapPodDevice`, `UnmapPodDevice` and `TearDownDevice` to check that there are no orphan files.

Some changes to fake CSI client were necessary to create / delete publish path by the fake driver.

/kind bug

issue_context.title: CSI block volume leaves orphan files
issue_context.body:
**What happened**:
When a pod that uses a CSI raw block volume is deleted, kubelet leaves some files in /var/lib/kubelet, without cleaning them.

```
/var/lib/kubelet/plugins/kubernetes.io/csi/volumeDevices/pvc-68ddc376-0d7d-4187-9911-c585cc6c8628/data/vol_data.json
/var/lib/kubelet/plugins/kubernetes.io/csi/volumeDevices/publish/pvc-68ddc376-0d7d-4187-9911-c585cc6c8628 (empty directory)
```

(where `pvc-68ddc376-0d7d-4187-9911-c585cc6c8628` is name of a PV used as a raw block volume.

**What you expected to happen**:
All files are cleaned up, only `/var/lib/kubelet/plugins/kubernetes.io/csi/volumeDevices/staging` and `/var/lib/kubelet/plugins/kubernetes.io/csi/volumeDevices/publish` remain, as they can contain files / directories of other raw block volumes.

**How to reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)**:
Run hostpath tests and check /var/lib/kubelet after the tests.

- Kubernetes version (use `kubectl version`): last week master, 641321c94c3e0943a57230596164e2e8f2eb2c52

/sig storage

review_comments: Do we need to introduce uncertain device tracking for block volume calls? We can do this in a follow up but we should track that work somewhere?
Wait is that correct? That is another PR..
sorry, I fixed my previous comment with the right link
nit: redundant cast to string for `nodeName`

If I understand correctly, `NodePublishVolume` for a block device should cause the device to show up in the host filesystem at target path (e.g. /dev/foo) while mounted devices should create a folder into which the volume gets mounted?

And in both cases, the implementation ("SP") is responsible for causing those paths to exist?

This is right. I seemed to forget to write down the existence of "data/vol_data.json" under xxx/plugins/kubernetes.io/csi/volumeDevices/<volume name> in L56 comments. 

Should we add a comment on the file, there?
Then, I think that everyone will be able to check that all paths are cleaned up properly, just by comparing the comments and this cleanup function.

Creating a temp dir will prevent this test from interfering with different runs, but should we care about different test cases running in their own directories?

side note: These tests should be wrapped with `t.Run` in the future.

The tests run in series right now, so I would leave it up to the guy who makes them parallel :-). Slightly more complicate refactoring would be needed then, as the target path is part of the test struct before any `t.Run`.
Seems like a good use case for `os.RemoveAll` unless we want to be very explicit about what gets deleted.
RemoveAll would remove also stuff that should be removed by GenerateUnmapVolumeFunc and we would not see this bug.

Ok, I added `RemoveAll()` there, this directory contains only "global" bind-mount and metadata json. It is not used in stage/publish/unpublish/unstage loop, where blind RemoveAll could hide hard to track unpublish / unstage errors.
Thanks, I didn't realize the subtle implications with reference to bind mount and GenerateUnmapVolumeFunc.
suggest using `: %v` for errors instead of `%s`
Any reason we used `os.Remove` and not `os.RemoveAll`? Are we comfortable assuming that all files inside the directory were deleted by a different function?
`Remove` is on the safe side. With our usage of bind mounts I don't want to accidentally remove stuff that was bind-mounted to a wrong place.
